# Vintage Records Meet Novel Technology: Using Artificial Intelligence to Find New Stories for America’s 250th Birthday | The Signal

## Vintage Records Meet Novel Technology: Using Artificial Intelligence to Find New Stories for America’s 250th Birthday

Posted by: [Leah Weinryb-Grohsgal](https://blogs.loc.gov/thesignal/author/lweinryb/)

This year libraries and cultural institutions around the nation are celebrating America’s 250 th birthday. The 225-year-old Library of Congress is almost as old as the country itself and this year we’ve joined forces with the Smithsonian Institution to find new stories about America’s founding in our treasure trove of records and artifacts.

The collaboration, called  [Revolution Crossroads](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/?loclr=blogsig) , is exploring how advanced technologies can surface new connections in history. Staff are working to expand the promise of artificial intelligence (AI) to surface relationships, stories, and context—using some of the nation’s founding digital treasures as a testbed.

Revolution Crossroads builds on vast collections of Revolutionary Era materials held by the Library, the Smithsonian, and other publicly available materials like those at the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). These holdings include newspaper articles, letters, military records, 3D objects, maps, artworks, and much more, making the possibilities for investigation using the power of AI especially enticing.

The initiative zooms in on some major sources of information about the Revolutionary Era—78,000 page-level historic newspaper records from  [Chronicling America](https://www.loc.gov/collections/chronicling-america/about-this-collection/?loclr=blogsig) , over 10,000 records about a variety of objects, artworks and documents from four  [Smithsonian museums](https://www.si.edu/?loclr=blogsig) , and more than 2 million pages of military and pension records held by the  [National Archives and Records Administration](https://www.archives.gov/?loclr=blogsig) . Using these collections, Smithsonian and Library staff are pulling together large-scale datasets to test what AI can do to help us tell new stories using preserved materials from the past.

These [datasets](https://huggingface.co/RevolutionCrossroads/?loclr=blogsig), created from Smithsonian Institution data, Library of Congress newspaper pages, and [National Archives Revolutionary War pension files](https://www.archives.gov/citizen-archivist/missions/revolutionary-war-pension-files/?loclr=blogsig), bring together materials to gain insights into our shared past. Putting these diverse collections—including military equipment, letters, postal route maps, miniature portraits, coins, garments, press reporting, pension records, and more—in conversation with one another using advanced technologies could provide glimpses into a fuller picture of the Revolutionary Era, including firsthand perspectives, everyday details, and insights into life after the Revolutionary War from communities across the United States.

AI technologies enable new ways of interacting with data and collections, allowing us to search, analyze, and organize information as never before. The rise of these methods raises new questions about how we access information and reveal connections: in these vast datasets, what people, networks, and features of daily life and famous events have not yet been discovered? The results may be surprising, and they may hold keys to [analyzing large historical record collections](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/printing-press-ai-back-again?loclr=blogsig) well beyond the 1770 to 1810 time period.

The Revolution Crossroads team is building on decades of technical work, a foundation created by the project’s core partners as well as other cultural heritage institutions around the world to preserve and provide access to digital collections. The data, while machine readable, requires structuring and shaping to make it accessible to AI tools. The team’s initial contribution was releasing AI-ready datasets on the Hugging Face open-source AI and machine learning platform. Each dataset includes an info card [providing a summary and description of the dataset](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/data-hug?loclr=blogsig), details about source and curation rationale, data collection and processing history, and supporting files and information.

The initiative has already brought new and engaging stories to the fore. Parsons School of Design Masters of Data Visualization students worked with Smithsonian, Library of Congress, and National Archives staff to visualize data in [nine projects](https://dv.parsons.edu/archive/?category=Major+Studio&year=2025/?loclr=blogsig) ranging from Revolutionary War Era pension applications to stamps to silhouette art—and [many more fascinating windows into the past](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/visualizing-revolution?loclr=blogsig).

The Revolution Crossroads project’s focus on exploring data and connections relies on new technology, but the longstanding expertise of curators, researchers, and staff are at its heart. This initiative extends beyond the semiquincentennial to one of the Library’s [core tenets](https://www.loc.gov/digital-strategy/artificial-intelligence/?loclr=blogsig) for working with Artificial Intelligence : balancing human judgment with machine capabilities. We hope you’ll check back at the Signal Blog and the  [Revolution Crossroads website](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/?loclr=blogsig)  for more information about what we find!

The Library of Congress is commemorating America’s 250 th  anniversary with many opportunities under the theme “It’s Your Story.” Read more about the Library’s America’s 250 activities, including exhibitions, collections-inspired programming, digital initiatives, and major initiatives with the Semiquincentennial Commission, in  [Library of Congress Celebrates America’s 250 Years](https://newsroom.loc.gov/news/library-of-congress-celebrates-america-s-250-years/s/f24d73a1-2beb-4ca8-bbb7-49ebc3f65145/?loclr=blogsig) .

# 舊藏紀錄遇上新穎科技：運用人工智慧為美國 250 週年尋找新故事 | The Signal

## 舊藏紀錄遇上新穎科技：運用人工智慧為美國 250 週年尋找新故事

作者：[Leah Weinryb-Grohsgal](https://blogs.loc.gov/thesignal/author/lweinryb/)

今年，全美各地的圖書館與文化機構都在慶祝美國 250 週年。已有 225 年歷史的美國國會圖書館，幾乎和這個國家本身一樣古老；今年，我們與史密森學會（Smithsonian Institution）攜手合作，要在我們珍貴的紀錄與文物寶庫中，尋找關於美國建國的新故事。

這項合作計畫名為 [Revolution Crossroads](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/?loclr=blogsig)，正在探索先進科技如何浮現歷史中的新連結。工作人員正努力拓展人工智慧（AI）的潛力，運用美國建國相關的一些數位珍藏作為測試場域，找出關係、故事與脈絡。

Revolution Crossroads 奠基於美國國會圖書館、史密森學會，以及其他公開可取用資料中大量的革命時期館藏，例如美國國家檔案暨文件署（NARA）的資料。這些館藏包括報紙文章、書信、軍事紀錄、3D 物件、地圖、藝術作品，以及更多資料；也因此，運用 AI 的力量進行探究的可能性格外令人期待。

這項計畫聚焦於革命時期幾個主要資訊來源——來自 [Chronicling America](https://www.loc.gov/collections/chronicling-america/about-this-collection/?loclr=blogsig) 的 78,000 筆以頁為單位的歷史報紙紀錄、來自四座[史密森博物館](https://www.si.edu/?loclr=blogsig)的超過 10,000 筆各類物件、藝術作品與文件紀錄，以及由[美國國家檔案暨文件署](https://www.archives.gov/?loclr=blogsig)保存的超過 200 萬頁軍事與撫卹金紀錄。透過這些館藏，史密森學會與國會圖書館的工作人員正在彙整大規模資料集，測試 AI 能如何協助我們運用過去保存下來的材料，講述新的故事。

這些由史密森尼學會資料、美國國會圖書館報紙頁面，以及[美國國家檔案館獨立戰爭撫卹金檔案](https://www.archives.gov/citizen-archivist/missions/revolutionary-war-pension-files/?loclr=blogsig)所建立的[資料集](https://huggingface.co/RevolutionCrossroads/?loclr=blogsig)，匯集多種材料，協助我們洞察共同的過去。透過先進技術，讓這些多元館藏相互對話，包括軍事裝備、書信、郵政路線圖、迷你肖像、錢幣、服飾、新聞報導、撫卹金紀錄等，或許能讓我們看見更完整的革命時代圖像，包括第一手觀點、日常生活細節，以及美國各地社群在獨立戰爭後生活樣貌的線索。

AI 技術帶來與資料和館藏互動的新方式，讓我們能以前所未有的方式搜尋、分析與整理資訊。這些方法的興起，也引發了關於我們如何取得資訊、揭示連結的新問題：在這些龐大的資料集中，還有哪些人物、網絡，以及日常生活和知名事件的特徵尚未被發現？結果可能令人意外，也可能為[分析大型歷史紀錄館藏](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/printing-press-ai-back-again?loclr=blogsig)提供關鍵線索，其適用範圍遠超過 1770 至 1810 年這段時期。

Revolution Crossroads 團隊奠基於數十年的技術工作；這項基礎由該專案的核心夥伴，以及世界各地其他文化遺產機構共同建立，用以保存數位館藏並提供取用。這些資料雖然可供機器讀取，但仍需要結構化與整理，才能讓 AI 工具使用。團隊的初步貢獻，是在 Hugging Face 開源 AI 與機器學習平台上發布 AI-ready 資料集。每個資料集都包含一張資訊卡，[提供資料集的摘要與說明](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/data-hug?loclr=blogsig)、來源與策展理由的細節、資料蒐集與處理歷程，以及支援檔案與相關資訊。

這項計畫已經帶出許多新穎且引人入勝的故事。Parsons School of Design 資料視覺化碩士班學生與史密森尼學會、美國國會圖書館和美國國家檔案館的工作人員合作，在[九個專案](https://dv.parsons.edu/archive/?category=Major+Studio&year=2025/?loclr=blogsig)中將資料視覺化，主題從美國獨立戰爭時期的年金申請、郵票，到剪影藝術，以及[更多引人入勝、通往過去的窗口](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/visualizing-revolution?loclr=blogsig)。

Revolution Crossroads 專案聚焦於探索資料與連結，這有賴新科技，但其核心是策展人、研究人員與工作人員長年累積的專業知識。這項計畫不只關乎 250 週年紀念，也延伸到國會圖書館運用人工智慧（Artificial Intelligence）的[核心信念](https://www.loc.gov/digital-strategy/artificial-intelligence/?loclr=blogsig)之一：在人的判斷與機器能力之間取得平衡。希望你持續回來關注 Signal Blog 和 [Revolution Crossroads 網站](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/?loclr=blogsig)，了解我們發現了什麼！

美國國會圖書館正以「這是你的故事」（It’s Your Story）為主題，透過多項活動紀念美國 250 週年。想進一步了解國會圖書館的 America’s 250 活動，包括展覽、由館藏啟發的節目、數位倡議，以及與 250 週年委員會（Semiquincentennial Commission）合作的重大計畫，請閱讀 [Library of Congress Celebrates America’s 250 Years](https://newsroom.loc.gov/news/library-of-congress-celebrates-america-s-250-years/s/f24d73a1-2beb-4ca8-bbb7-49ebc3f65145/?loclr=blogsig)。

這項計畫已經帶出許多新穎且引人入勝的故事。Parsons School of Design 資料視覺化碩士班學生與史密森尼學會、美國國會圖書館和美國國家檔案館的工作人員合作，在[九個專案](https://dv.parsons.edu/archive/?category=Major+Studio&year=2025/?loclr=blogsig)中將資料視覺化，主題從美國獨立戰爭時期的年金申請、郵票，到剪影藝術，以及[更多引人入勝、通往過去的窗口](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/visualizing-revolution?loclr=blogsig)。

Revolution Crossroads 專案聚焦於探索資料與連結，這有賴新科技，但其核心是策展人、研究人員與工作人員長年累積的專業知識。這項計畫不只關乎 250 週年紀念，也延伸到國會圖書館運用人工智慧（Artificial Intelligence）的[核心信念](https://www.loc.gov/digital-strategy/artificial-intelligence/?loclr=blogsig)之一：在人的判斷與機器能力之間取得平衡。希望你持續回來關注 Signal Blog 和 [Revolution Crossroads 網站](https://www.si.edu/revolution-crossroads/?loclr=blogsig)，了解我們發現了什麼！

美國國會圖書館正以「這是你的故事」（It’s Your Story）為主題，透過多項活動紀念美國 250 週年。想進一步了解國會圖書館的 America’s 250 活動，包括展覽、由館藏啟發的節目、數位倡議，以及與 250 週年委員會（Semiquincentennial Commission）合作的重大計畫，請閱讀 [Library of Congress Celebrates America’s 250 Years](https://newsroom.loc.gov/news/library-of-congress-celebrates-america-s-250-years/s/f24d73a1-2beb-4ca8-bbb7-49ebc3f65145/?loclr=blogsig)。
